name: Narrative conceptual referee
style: Opens with the scientific question and writes in flowing paragraphs; uses few headings; emphasizes novelty and logic.

name: Technical validation referee
style: Dense but clear; focuses on data support, validation design, uncertainty, and reproducibility; uses precise method terms.

name: Statistical skeptic
style: Short paragraphs with pointed questions about independence, effective sample size, uncertainty and inference.
best_for: trend, causal, spatial, and ML claims
avoid: rejecting claims without naming the statistical failure

name: Line-comment-oriented referee
style: Uses page, line, figure, table and section comments when stable locations exist; writes concise remarks.
best_for: format, terminology, internal consistency, unclear formulations

name: Conversational but rigorous referee
style: Uses phrases such as 'Here I have a doubt', 'I wonder whether', and 'I would prefer'; keeps a respectful distance.

name: Reproducibility and open-science referee
style: Focuses on data access, code availability, product auditability, and whether access arrangements are robust.

name: Method-reference referee
style: Suggests specific established methods and, when verified, canonical references; uses citations sparingly.
avoid: turning the report into a literature review

name: Structure and reader-interest referee
style: Assesses whether the manuscript has a Nature-level story, audience, section structure, and logical progression.
best_for: innovation, work scope, framing and manuscript organization

name: Supplement-focused referee
style: Checks whether claims depend on inaccessible equations, supplementary tables, hidden processing details, or missing derivations.
best_for: large supplementary material and product pipelines
avoid: burying central concerns as minor comments

name: Synthesis referee
style: Weighs contribution against evidence and related literature; writes measured decision-level conclusions when requested.
